pangenome/hprc_cfhr_deletion.name: pangenome/hprc_cfhr_deletion
pangenome/hprc_cfhr_deletion.note: do you think the bandage graph intuitively shows the deletion here? could it be better? cross reference other graph drawing programs to see if it could ANSWERED: no, it did not, and the figure is now the anchored layout instead of the force one. WHY THE FORCE DRAWING COULD NOT DO IT, measured off the capture rather than argued: FMMM has no reference axis, so the arc's two endpoints are wherever the simulation put them and its size is the only thing left to carry the event. Two things followed. The arc bowed out by the drawn length of the backbone it bypasses, but that backbone was scattered across the drawing, so the big black loop enclosed nothing; and the label rides an apex computed from the BYPASSED nodes (deletionApex in graphLabels.ts) while the curve is drawn between the EDGE's endpoints, which in a force layout are different places -- 'skips 84.7 kb of reference' sat top right on the magenta chain with the loop sweeping the opposite corner. The two agree in an anchored layout, which is why nobody had noticed. CROSS-REFERENCED AGAINST ~/src/vendor, as asked. Every tool that shows a deletion legibly puts the reference on an axis first. VRPG (lh3's rGFA viewer) projects the graph onto reference coordinates beside a linear annotation panel, which is this pairing. sequenceTubeMap orders nodes monotonically along x with a width per node from its length, so a path that skips nodes is drawn across the nodes it skips (drawDeletion in tubemap.js is a grey line over exactly that span). odgi does not use a node-link drawing for this at all: odgi pav / odgi viz reduce presence/absence to a path-by-position matrix where a deletion is a gap in one row. Bandage has no reference concept, so a deletion there is a bare link at a joint with nothing to state, and our bulge was already an improvement on it. PangyPlot is the one force-directed pangenome viewer that solves it, and it does the inverse of what we did: the deletion link stays a straight chord with an x at its midpoint, and a dedicated force (delLinkForce in layout-forces.js) pushes the bypassed nodes perpendicularly off it, so the LAYOUT closes the bubble instead of the edge bowing to fake one. WHAT CHANGED: layoutMode auto, bubbleSpread dropped (it is a floor in FMMM units passed to the remote engine only, so it was dead under a local layout and only added a no-op step to the figure's recipe), viewportHeight 1580 -> 1342 for the shorter pane. The arc now spans exactly the bp it removes and spans them under the hg38 row above, so the boxed CFHR3/CFHR1, the carrier's missing ribbon and the arc line up on the same coordinates. Cost, stated in the spec and the caption: MIN_DELETION_LABEL_PX gates on the arc's bulge in screen px, and at 0.4% the other two deletions (2.2 kb, 9.3 kb) come to ~13 px, so they draw as short thick arcs without labels where in FMMM units they had them. ON YOUR FOLLOW-UP ("should it literally just draw it as a lineargenomeview track?", then "we could make a custom track type also ... but this could be misguided, based on idea of linearizing the pangenome, which gave us a lot of heartache before"): agreed, and DECIDED AGAINST rather than left open, written up in agent-docs/reference/PANGENOME_GRAPHS.md under Carriage. It is buildable and cheap -- links.bed.gz already states both endpoints with ranks, deletionEdges.ts already classifies them, BedpeAdapter and LinearPairedArcDisplay ship in core, so no new hosted file and no build-script change would be needed. Three reasons not to. A backbone-to-backbone skip names no donor, so the arcs are anonymous, and a row in a linear track reads as carriage: the same misreading that retired hprc_allele_inventory's sample rows. wave.vcf.gz already draws this event better, with no plugin at all -- not symbolic, tabix-indexed, explicit ALTs to 65 kb, a genotype per haplotype, and this deletion is one of its records at 139 of 464 haplotypes; a projected arc is that with the genotypes discarded. And what the projection would uniquely add over the VCF is segment-level correspondence plus the chaining and nesting of an alternate path, and nesting is exactly the part an axis cannot hold, so the content worth linearizing is already in the VCF and the rest is not linearizable. The anchored figure stands: it puts the graph on the reference axis for reading, without claiming the graph states carriage.

pangenome/graph_context.name: pangenome/graph_context
pangenome/graph_context.note: previous agent notes, please re-review this: this is good to show now, but to some extent it makes me wonder (a) why we wouldn't default to more hops and (b) whether this can be illustrated better and (c) what the gui is for selecting this, user might not intuitively understand ANSWERED, (c) fixed in code, and (a) is HALF AN EXCUSE, so it is written down as such. (a) NOT AN EXCUSE, and now FIXED IN THE PLUGIN (commit ce96cd5, NOT deployed, see the handoff at the end). Cross-referenced against ~/src/vendor per your ask, and all three tools disagree with what we were doing. gfabase sub expands from a seed either to the whole connected component (--connected, which its own README calls overkill) or with --cutpoints 1, which takes the biconnected component by stopping at cutpoints, the segments every end-to-end walk of the chromosome must traverse. gfatools view -R never hops at all: it maps the region onto a precomputed bubble decomposition and returns whole overlapping bubbles (gfa_query_by_reg in gfa-util.c), complete by construction. Bandage's own --distance IS a node-step radius, but Bandage holds the whole graph in memory, so its scope is a drawing filter rather than a fetch strategy. Everyone stops at the structural boundary. We were stopping at a coordinate frontier. SO TWO CHANGES. A hop now follows off-reference segments only, which is gfabase's stop-at-cutpoints rule with the rank tag standing in for a connectivity index (in a reference-anchored pangenome the cutpoints ARE the backbone, and rank already says which segments those are). And the default is now 1 rather than 0, because at 0 the drawing is wrong and not merely sparse. MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, same windows. Old rule: paa 14 segments at 0, 20 at 1, 27 at 2 and still climbing, 4 of the 7 that 2 added being K12 backbone outside the window plus a 39,851 bp Sakai segment. New rule: paa 14 at 0, 17 at 1, 17 at 2, so the cut closes and STAYS closed, and the off-window backbone stubs are gone from the picture. HPRC amylase 63 / 78 / 92, which does keep growing, but in the right dimension (its alleles have alleles) rather than by walking the reference away. Wall-clock is flat across all three settings on both graphs, a hop's queries going out together against an index that dominates, so cost was never the real argument for the old default. WHAT IS STILL TRUE from the old answer: a frontier is not a bubble decomposition, so this is closer to complete rather than complete. The exact version is available with data we already ship, and is written up in the adapter: gfatools bubble rows carry the member segment ids of each bubble, and MinigraphBubbleAdapter already parses them, so the bubbles overlapping a region state exactly which segments a complete cut must contain. That turns the hop count into a termination condition instead of a setting. (b) BETTER ILLUSTRATED is what this round did (see below). Considered and rejected: a third panel at 2 hops. It would be a wider tangle whose growth is off-window, so the panel could not show its own difference, and the compose already repeats the linear view per half, so a third would make it 2250px of mostly duplicate content. (c) THE GUI was a real gap and is fixed durably. The figure's recipe dialog (the ? beside the live link) had no click-path for any GraphGenomeView field, so a reader got the session JSON and no menu at all. Seven fields now map, against labels read off the pinned plugin bundle rather than guessed: the launch itself (Track menu -> Launch view -> Graph genome view (this region)), the window, Layout, Color, Bubble spread, Reference path, and Graph context. The dialog's last step now reads 'Graph view menu -> Settings -> Graph context -> 1 hop', which is exactly the question. The guide also spells the menu out in all three places it names a graph setting (View menu -> Settings -> ...), where it had said only 'Settings -> ...'. previous notes: I don't particularly understand the difference here.  ideally, shows red boxes and arrow and/or text annotation showing the difference between the two sides. FIXED, both parts. Each half now carries the setting it is in a label (Graph context: None / 1 hop), which nothing in the frame said before, and both halves box THE SAME TWO NODES: 43 bp (s2093) and 558 bp (s2095), where one CFT073 detour leaves the K12 backbone and rejoins it. At None those two boxes are loose ends. At 1 hop they are the two sides of a closed bubble, and the arrow points at the 5.5 kb interior (s2094) the extra queries found, which is the whole of what the setting buys. Boxed by segment id through the view's own nodePositions, not by pixel, so FMMM can lay the two halves out as differently as it likes. Why it was unreadable before: the two layouts share no visible landmark, so the change was stated only as a node count in the header (14 nodes/15 edges against 20/25) over two tangles. Caption updated to name the boxes and the arrow, and to say why the right half still has loose ends of its own. DEPLOY HANDOFF, the one thing left. The plugin change is committed but NOT published, so the hosted bundle and every figure in this repo still show the old behaviour, and the guide still says the default is None, which is currently true. betabuild.sh gates on lint + typecheck + tests and typecheck is red right now for a reason unrelated to this change: the plugin resolves @jbrowse/* through symlinks into this worktree, which has uncommitted core edits (configuration, PluginManager, BaseTrackModel), and model.test.ts fails to load for the same reason. Proven inherited by running both against plugin HEAD in a temp worktree, where they fail identically. That gate is exactly the one that catches a bundle importing a host global that does not exist, so it should not be skipped. Once the core tree is committed and it goes green: pnpm betabuild, bump the pinned esmUrl in the three test_data/graphgenomeview configs, regenerate every graph figure, and update the guide's default and the 2 hops paragraph, which the new rule makes stale.
